purpose: Tolcapone is used to help treat Parkinson's disease. It is used along with two other medicines called levodopa and carbidopa to help control the symptoms of Parkinson's, such as stiffness, tremors, and difficulty moving. It is typically prescribed when other treatments have not worked well enough on their own.
how_it_works: In your body, a chemical called COMT breaks down levodopa before it can reach your brain, making it less effective. Tolcapone blocks this COMT enzyme, so levodopa stays in your body longer and works better. Think of it as stopping a 'cleanup crew' that was removing your medicine too quickly, so the medicine can do its job for a longer time.
common_side_effects: Nausea, diarrhea (which can be severe), stomach pain, dizziness, drowsiness, trouble sleeping, increased sweating, muscle pain, headache, and a harmless orange-yellow discoloration of your urine. Some patients may also notice involuntary movements (called dyskinesia) as levodopa becomes more active in the body.
warnings: IMPORTANT: Tolcapone can cause serious, potentially life-threatening liver damage. Your doctor must monitor your liver with blood tests regularly, especially in the first six months of treatment. Contact your doctor immediately if you notice yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe stomach pain, or unusual fatigue. This medicine also carries a rare risk of a dangerous condition called neuroleptic malignant syndrome if stopped suddenly — never stop taking it without talking to your doctor first. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, as tolcapone can interact with several drugs.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 100 mg taken three times a day, along with your levodopa and carbidopa doses. Your doctor may increase this to 200 mg three times a day if needed and if your liver tests remain normal. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes, and never skip or stop doses without checking with your doctor first.
